newsitem.title: LEBANON: Moody's gives Lebanon B1 rating - finance minister.
newsitem.headline: Moody's gives Lebanon B1 rating - finance minister.

text.p: Moody's has assigned Lebanon a B1 credit rating and Nippon a triple B-, acting finance minister Fouad Siniora said on Wednesday.

Asked by Reuters to comment on announcements that IBCA had awarded Lebanon a BB rating and Standard and Poor's had awarded a BB minus, Siniora said "the others are coming up. Moody's B1 and Nippon triple B minus."
"There will be a statement by the ministry of finance in half an hour," Siniora added.

A statement issued by Merrill Lynch International quoted a Lebanese government spokesman saying "we feel that this is an important part of the continuing rehabilitation of the country both domestically and internationally and of the effort to increase the potential resources which could be mobilised for reconstruction and investment."
The statement said the ratings were the first awarded to Lebanon's long-term foreign currency debt obligations by the major international credit agencies.
"In addition, local currency ratings of BBB- and BB have been assigned by IBCA and S&P, respectively," Merrill Lynch said.
